items.stem: A team must answer questions about one 600,000-token report in a single request. The team uses Claude Opus 5.5 and expects an answer of about 8,000 tokens. Which design meets the constraint?
options: Split the report into chunks and send one request for each chunk.
Send the full report in one request and set max_tokens to 8,000.
Send the full report in one request with server-side compaction enabled on every turn.
Set max_tokens to 1,000,000 so the window holds the full report.
items.rationale: The context window holds the input and the new output of a turn. Opus 5.5 has a 1M-token window, so the report fits, and max_tokens caps only the output at 8,000.
items.trap: Setting max_tokens to 1,000,000 looks like a window fix, but max_tokens caps only the output of a response.

items.stem: A team deploys Claude Haiku 5.5 on Claude Platform on AWS. The application must send the model ID that this platform uses. Which choice meets the constraint?
options: The ID claude-haiku-5-5, the same ID that the Claude API uses.
A custom alias that a config service resolves to a model ID on each request.
The Foundry deployment name, which this platform uses in place of a model ID.
The Bedrock-style ID anthropic.claude-haiku-5-5 in the model field.
items.rationale: This platform reuses the first-party model IDs, with no Bedrock-style prefix. Claude Haiku 5.5 therefore uses claude-haiku-5-5 here.
items.trap: The Bedrock-style ID looks right for Haiku 5.5, but this platform omits the anthropic prefix.

items.stem: A support app lets Claude look up order status through a tool. The app must run each lookup in its own code behind its permission checks. Which two options meet the constraint?
options: Return each result as a tool_result block with the next request.
Let the model call the order API directly with its own network access.
Set stop_reason to tool_result so the loop continues.
Repeat the request while stop_reason is tool_use, and exit on end_turn.
items.rationale: The app runs each tool and returns its output as a tool_result block. The loop repeats while stop_reason is tool_use and exits on the other documented stop reasons.
items.trap: Setting stop_reason to tool_result looks like a loop control, but tool_result is a block type that the app sends, not a stop reason.
